root_idea.summary: The root centers on turning aside with deviation, wavering, or retreat.
root_idea.development: From physical or behavioral turning away, the semantic range extends to retreat, flight, avoidance, and escape; the idiom حَيْصَ بَيْصَ applies the notion of being unable to find a way out to confusion or severe straitness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized classical citation form مَحِيصٌ as a verbal noun.

senses.definition: A place or way of escape; a refuge or way out.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the form denotes an available escape or refuge, often in constructions with مِنْ meaning that there is no escape from something; contextual renderings include “place of escape,” “place of refuge,” and “any escape.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of turning away, retreating, or fleeing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical infinitive use of the same form, distinct from its Quran-attested noun-of-place sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn away, retreat, or flee from something; figuratively, to deviate from the truth; also to avoid a thing and thereby become safe from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عن and in contexts of withdrawal from combat or an adversary, flight, deviation, or avoidance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deal with someone by artifice or guile; to vie with or strive to overcome him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction describing adversarial maneuvering or competition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of confusion, severe straitness, or difficulty from which there is no escape; figuratively, being so hemmed in that one cannot act freely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression that may describe falling into difficulty or putting someone in circumstances where movement, livelihood, or free action is restricted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hole of a rat or mouse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate lexical use of the fixed expression, not the idiom for confusion or straitness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skittish, wayward beast that takes fright and runs off at random; especially, a badly behaved mule.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes an animal that turns away from what its master wants.

cautions: The Quranic contextual renderings “place of escape,” “place of refuge,” and “any escape” are treated as one escape/refuge sense rather than separate meanings.
The Classical infinitive use of مَحِيصٌ is listed separately from the Quranic noun-of-place use.
